standard.name: Neuroscience Information eXchange format (NIX)
standard.abstract: NIX is a generic data model and file-library for storing fully annotated neuroscience datasets — primarily developed for electrophysiology — that places experimental data together with rich metadata in the same container. Implementations typically use HDF5 as the storage backend. The model represents multidimensional recordings (time series, spike trains, images, etc.) plus points/regions of interest and annotations (odML) so files can be self-describing and machine-readable.

classification.rationale: NIX is primarily a data model with an explicit entity-relationship (DAG) describing Blocks, DataArrays, Dimensions, Tags, etc., but the documentation also defines concrete metadata/data fields (DataArray fields, Dimension descriptors, file-format version triplet) that are naturally represented as a metadata table. Both representations are supported; table is prioritized because the spec lists concrete fields and their semantics.

purpose.name: purpose
purpose.descr: Overall aim / scope of the format
purpose.evidence: "The NIX data model allows to store fully annotated scientific datasets, i.e. the data together with its metadata within the same container."

backend.name: storage_backend
backend.descr: On-disk storage backend used by implementations
backend.evidence: "The current implementations store the actual data using the HDF5 file format as a storage backend."

dataarray_entity.name: DataArray (entity)
dataarray_entity.descr: Central data container storing numeric/multidimensional data plus labels/units and dimensions
dataarray_entity.evidence: "The DataArray is the most central entity of the NIX data model."

dataarray_name_type_uniqueness.name: DataArray:name,type,uniqueness
dataarray_name_type_uniqueness.descr: Naming and typing requirements for DataArray
dataarray_name_type_uniqueness.evidence: "As almost all other NIX-entities it requires a name and a type. Both are not restricted but names must be unique inside a Block."

dataarray_data_label_unit.name: DataArray:data,label,unit
dataarray_data_label_unit.descr: DataArray stores the actual data together with descriptive label and unit
dataarray_data_label_unit.evidence: "The DataArray stores the actual data together with label and unit."

dimensions_overview.name: Dimensions (overview)
dimensions_overview.descr: Kinds of dimension descriptors that must be provided for each DataArray dimension
dimensions_overview.evidence: "In NIX we define three (and a half) dimension descriptors:"

sampled_dimension.name: SampledDimension
sampled_dimension.descr: Descriptor for regularly sampled dimensions (e.g. time series). Stores sampling interval, offset, label, unit
sampled_dimension.evidence: "SampledDimension: Used if a dimension is sampled at regular intervals."

sampled_axis_parameters.name: SampledDimension:parameters
sampled_axis_parameters.descr: Parameters needed to describe a sampled axis
sampled_axis_parameters.evidence: "The x-axis can be fully described with just a few parameters: sampling interval offset label unit"

range_dimension.name: RangeDimension
range_dimension.descr: Descriptor for irregularly sampled dimensions; stores explicit ticks/positions
range_dimension.evidence: "RangeDimension: Used if a dimension is sampled at irregular intervals."

alias_range_dimension.name: AliasRangeDimension
alias_range_dimension.descr: Special RangeDimension tied to DataArray values (useful for event times); constraints apply
alias_range_dimension.evidence: "A special case of a RangeDimension that is used when storing something equivalent to event times."

alias_range_constraint.name: AliasRangeDimension:constraint
alias_range_constraint.descr: AliasRangeDimension is only permitted for 1-D numeric data
alias_range_constraint.evidence: "Note! An AliasRangeDimension is only permitted if the data is 1-D and the values are numeric, an exception will be thrown otherwise."

set_dimension.name: SetDimension
set_dimension.evidence: "SetDimension: Used for dimensions that represent categories rather than physical quantities."

tag_multitag.name: Tag / MultiTag
tag_multitag.descr: Entities to tag points or regions in DataArrays; applied positions/extents are used to retrieve slices
tag_multitag.evidence: "Tags and MultiTags refer to DataArrays to tag points or regions in the data."

block_entity.name: Block (container)
block_entity.descr: Container grouping named entities; name uniqueness scoped to Block
block_entity.evidence: "names must be unique inside a Block."

file_versioning.name: File format versioning
file_versioning.descr: File-format uses an X.Y.Z triplet semantics to indicate compatibility and breaking changes
file_versioning.evidence: "The file format is versioned with a triplet of integers, that carries semantics, thus can and indeed must be used by libraries that want to open NIX files to determine if the version of the file is compatible with the library version (i.e. the file can be read or written to)."

position_matching.name: PositionMatching rules
position_matching.descr: Rules for converting positions to indices along dimensions (Less, LessOrEqual, Equal, GreaterOrEqual, Greater)
position_matching.evidence: "Five possible rules of PositionMatching ... 1. Less ... 2. LessOrEqual ... 3. Equal ... 4. GreaterOrEqual ... 5. Greater"

range_matching_inclusive_exclusive.name: RangeMatch behavior
range_matching_inclusive_exclusive.descr: Ranges can be inclusive or exclusive; default behavior differs by version
range_matching_inclusive_exclusive.evidence: "In version 1.4.x ranges along a dimension are inclusive ... With NIX version 1.4.5 (nixpy 1.4.9x) we allow to choose which behavior is desired."

dataframe_entity.name: DataFrame (tabular)
dataframe_entity.descr: Tabular data object introduced to represent columns/rows (metadata table support)
dataframe_entity.evidence: "A new object type called DataFrame for tabular data."

odml_annotation.name: odML metadata annotation
odml_annotation.descr: Support for annotating all data elements with odML metadata model
odml_annotation.evidence: "All data elements can be annotated with additional metadata using the odML data model (Grewe et al. 2011), which is an intrinsic part of the model specification."

type_annotation_domain_support.name: Type annotation / domain mapping
type_annotation_domain_support.descr: Model is domain-agnostic but supports type annotation to represent domain-specific entities
type_annotation_domain_support.evidence: "The data model by design is not domain specific, but supports type annotation, providing the means to represent data in the generic model  as domain specific entities."
